Single-pixel images, edge and corner starts, and disconnected same-color regions work naturally; diagonal-only connections remain unchanged. For N pixels, copying and traversal take O(N) time and O(N) space.

Marker: INTERVIEW-84-e03f610d375ef664.

Approach: use breadth-first search from the top-left zero cell, exploring all eight neighboring directions. Track visited cells separately, marking them when enqueued, and start at distance 1 because path length counts cells. Return the distance when reaching the bottom-right; return -1 if the queue empties.

Invariant: BFS processes cells in nondecreasing distance, so each cell’s first discovery gives its shortest path length. Marking on enqueue prevents duplicate processing.

Boundary cases: either endpoint blocked means -1; a single zero cell returns 1, while a single one returns -1. Diagonal moves are allowed, even between blocked orthogonal neighbors. Unreachable destinations return -1; an empty grid, if permitted, also returns -1.

For an n × n grid, time and space are O(n²).
